A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2D research, with matching algorithms, theoretical guarantees and proofs. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical results and symbolic comparisons of published noise guarantees, but no original empirical outcomes. Its conclusion explicitly leaves experiments to future work.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original classification, unlearning, membership-inference and runtime results on eICU and Lacuna-100.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the core checkpoint, gradient-descent and Gaussian-perturbation procedure. However, v1 leaves stochastic adaptation to future work, whereas v2 Section 4.2 implements shuffling SGD, exponentially decaying step sizes and alternative noise calibration for epsilon > 1. These are limited practical adaptations of R2D.

E1.justification: v2 introduces eICU hospital-stay classification and binary gender classification on VGGFace2-derived Lacuna-100, using MAAD-Face annotations. Evaluation removes selected users' data and includes unseen-user datasets for membership-inference attacks. v1 evaluates no datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 actually implements and evaluates Constrained Newton Step (CNS, Zhang et al., 2024) and Hessian-Free unlearning (HF, Qiao et al., 2024), including accuracy, membership-inference and runtime comparisons. v1 only discusses their properties and published guarantees. Langevin unlearning remains unevaluated.

E3.justification: The new experiments introduce MLP and ResNet-18 configurations, deletion of approximately 1–2% of data, validation-based model selection, and privacy/rewind sweeps with delta = 0.1. Membership inference uses logistic regression, AUROC, repeated cross-validation with 100 or 5 folds, and class-balanced unseen-user controls. These protocols have no experimental counterpart in v1.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds sensitivity analyses of rewind length and privacy/noise settings, including comparison of the new rewind bound with numerical solutions. Appendix D.3 and Figure 3 test whether rewinding without Gaussian noise reduces membership-inference scores. v1 contains no corresponding empirical analyses or ablations.

E5.justification: v2 introduces five-seed averages for the tradeoff and noiseless analyses. Appendix D.1 specifies seeds 0–4, baseline comparisons using only seed 1, and reuse of rescaled Gaussian noise within each seed. This adds basic repeated-run reporting, without confidence intervals or significance tests; v1 reports no empirical statistics.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive error, membership-inference and runtime results. For example, Table 8 reports eICU test errors of 0.4675 for R2D with 41% rewinding, 0.5588 for CNS and 0.3125 for HF at epsilon = 40 and delta = 0.1. These are newly reported comparisons, with no empirical results in v1 to replace.

T1.justification: v2 adds Corollary 3.2 and its Appendix B.3 proof, bounding rewind length for fixed noise and privacy parameters. Theorem 3.1 now restricts epsilon to 0 < epsilon <= 1, and Appendix C revises the bounded-radius Gaussian-noise expression. The principal unlearning and PL results remain substantially unchanged after matching relocated and renumbered material.

C1.justification: v2 expands the theoretical contributions with claims of a novel, realistic user-level unlearning framework and empirical advantages over existing methods. Its conclusion newly claims superiority in storage, computation, accuracy and unlearning. These substantially broaden v1's algorithmic and theoretical claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of distributional confounding in membership-inference scores, limitations of forgetting-error metrics, practical departures from the theory, and baselines' training-versus-unlearning costs. It also interprets the noiseless results. Conversely, v1's explicit concluding caveat about checkpoint storage and full-data access for checkpoint reconstruction is omitted.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds architecture adjustments, hyperparameter tables, gradient/smoothness estimation procedures, model-selection instructions, hardware/software versions and an anonymized code link. These greatly expand reproducibility information. However, its printed smoothness estimator divides parameter distance by gradient distance, reversing the ratio implied by the stated gradient-Lipschitz condition.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for federated unlearning, analytical Gaussian calibration, datasets, membership inference and smooth activations. It also emphasizes storage costs and distinguishes user-level deletion from class-based or uniformly sampled deletion. The central positioning against D2D, Langevin, CNS and HF remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and conclusion and reorganizes the introduction around empirical contributions. The main-text prior-work comparison is consolidated with old Appendix A into Appendix C, while the proximal lemma proof moves into a new Appendix A. These substantially change the narrative and organization beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, introduces three multi-panel figures and seven additional tables, and redesigns Table 1 to include storage complexity. v1's noise-comparison Table 2 becomes Appendix Table 3, incorporating the bounded-parameter column. Both new displays and substantial redistribution of existing material change presentation.

improvement.justification: v2's experiments, runtime measurements and detailed protocols make v1's practical claims more assessable. However, Appendix D.1 prints an inverted smoothness-estimation ratio, leaving noise calibration uncertain; the PDFs cannot establish whether this is merely typographical or affected the experiments. Section 5's broad superiority claim also exceeds the mixed findings in Tables 2, 8 and 9. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
